newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss agree extradition of Rwanda tribunal suspect.
newsitem.headline: Swiss agree extradition of Rwanda tribunal suspect.

text.p: Switzerland is ready to comply with a request for the extradition of Alfred Musema after a United Nations tribunal indicted him for genocide in Rwanda, justice offficials said on Tuesday.
Musema, a former director of a tea factory in Gisuvu, in Rwanda's Kibuye province, has been held in Switzerland since February 1995.

Switzerland's Federal Police Affairs Office (BAP) said it had ruled in favour of extradition, giving Musema 30 days to appeal to the high court against being sent to the United Nations tribunal in the Tanzanian city of Arusha.
The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda was set up to try leaders of the 1994 genocide by Hutus of up to one million Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
It indicted Musema in July on charges of genocide and crimes against humanity and asked Switzerland to extradite him.
The Swiss police office, an agency of the justice ministry, said Musema had 30 days to lodge an appeal with the Federal High Court.
He could be extradited sooner if his lawyers decline to appeal in the first five days after receiving a written copy of the decision, an agency spokesman told reporters.
Musema had been in Switzerland applying for political asylum when he was arrested after private informers told Swiss police of his suspected role in Rwanda, according to Swiss media.
